species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band does NOT apply: no sourced launch-speed spread for this animal, so the launch speed is NOT drawn and stays at the engine's own value. The spread below therefore comes only from mass, area and the wave terms.

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

Inside the range, but PARTLY CIRCULAR: the 15 m/s take-off speed comes from the same body of observations (15-20 m/s) as the 50 m glide. Not independent evidence. the scenario's own modelCard says so: Cheilopogon (Cypselurus) heterurus doederleini - makiguchi-2013. Consistent; not a pass/fail test Validity stated by the model: Flying-fish-sized gliders (0.02-0.4 kg), mean-chord Re 5e3-1e5, launch heights 0-10 m. The polar is from stuffed specimens at one wind speed (12 m/s; Park & Choi: Re ~1e4); a zebrafish-sized or larval animal is far outside it (inRange false), and cannot reach its v_min anyway. OUT OF VALIDITY for this organism: Mass 0.0006943 kg is outside 0.02-0.4 kg (polar specimens 0.04-0.06 kg; field fliers to ~0.4 kg): polar extrapolated. Mean-chord Reynolds number ~4.6e+3 is outside 5e3-1e5 around the polar's Re ~1e4 (Park & Choi: 'gliding flying fish (Re ~10^4)'; air kinematic viscosity 1.46e-5 m2/s). glide_range_total_m exceeds the Lean bound whenever the kinetic phase is non-zero; only glide_range_lean_bound_m is covered by glide_range_le. Fick bound: arterial PO2 taken equal to air PO2 and gills taken to work in air; gills do not ventilate in air (physiology chain), so for a gill-breather this is a generous upper bound. TFF: NOTES-FOR-HUB.md item 2 says only 29.5% of the flight muscle the simulator charges fits in the body. This module uses no muscle power (the Fick bound is the cap), so the issue does not enter here; any muscle-based claim for the TFF must take it into account.

Not independent evidence. the scenario's own modelCard says so: Cheilopogon (Cypselurus) heterurus doederleini - makiguchi-2013. Consistent; not a pass/fail test Assumed inputs: C_Lmax 0.78 is measured on a stuffed Cypselurus hiraii in a wind tunnel; using it for any other body is borrowed. Validity stated by the model: Flying-fish-sized gliders (0.02-0.4 kg), mean-chord Re 5e3-1e5, launch heights 0-10 m. The polar is from stuffed specimens at one wind speed (12 m/s; Park & Choi: Re ~1e4); a zebrafish-sized or larval animal is far outside it (inRange false), and cannot reach its v_min anyway. OUT OF VALIDITY for this organism: Mass 0.0006943 kg is outside 0.02-0.4 kg (polar specimens 0.04-0.06 kg; field fliers to ~0.4 kg): polar extrapolated. Mean-chord Reynolds number ~4.6e+3 is outside 5e3-1e5 around the polar's Re ~1e4 (Park & Choi: 'gliding flying fish (Re ~10^4)'; air kinematic viscosity 1.46e-5 m2/s). glide_range_total_m exceeds the Lean bound whenever the kinetic phase is non-zero; only glide_range_lean_bound_m is covered by glide_range_le. Fick bound: arterial PO2 taken equal to air PO2 and gills taken to work in air; gills do not ventilate in air (physiology chain), so for a gill-breather this is a generous upper bound. TFF: NOTES-FOR-HUB.md item 2 says only 29.5% of the flight muscle the simulator charges fits in the body. This module uses no muscle power (the Fick bound is the cap), so the issue does not enter here; any muscle-based claim for the TFF must take it into account.

equations: Ucrit(T, age) = k(age) x SL x r(T); k = 15.5 SL/s for >= 28 dpf (Plaut 2000), 10.5 SL/s at 14 dpf (Umax 12.1 / 1.15), linear between; 0.03 m/s at 5 dpf, linear to 14 dpf

Umax = 1.15 Ucrit; feasible (hold station) = current <= Ucrit; survives = null
Re = rho U SL / mu; C_D = 1.33 Re^-0.5 (Re < 5e5) or 0.072 Re^-0.2, on wetted area
D = 0.5 rho C_D S_wet U^2 (lower bound); P_red = f_myo f_red m 134 x 1.88^((T-20)/10) W
U_bound: 0.5 rho C_D(U) S_wet U^3 = P_red (upper bound on sustained speed)

model_honesty.statement: STUDIO-FINDINGS.md's one honest sentence applies to everything above: every numeric wild-type value that lands in band is read straight from the paper it is scored against. The negative controls (a zebrafish that cannot glide, a wingless flying fish that cannot glide, a TFF that cannot pay for powered flight) are the part of this result that is NOT circular, because they turn on inequalities between independently sourced quantities rather than on a fitted number.

physics_simulation.scope: Whether the design DOES the function asked of it, measured by running the engine's own scenario modules. It is not a validity claim and it is not a statement that the design is biologically possible: lean_check says no law is broken (necessary, not sufficient) and this says the function is or is not achieved in the model. Every check carries the validation status of the model behind it, and a check whose model is `circular` -- scored against a number read back from the paper it is compared with -- is not evidence however green it looks. The ensemble is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION over stated input distributions, most of whose shapes are assumed; it is not a measured distribution of real behaviour. Control, flapping, unsteady aerodynamics, take-off power, adhesion and whole-body stability are not modelled anywhere in this engine.

report.gates_note: lean_check says the design BREAKS NO LAW, which is necessary and not sufficient. physics_simulation says whether it ACTUALLY DOES THE THING. Neither substitutes for the other, and neither is folded into the score.

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band does NOT apply: no sourced launch-speed spread for this animal, so the launch speed is NOT drawn and stays at the engine's own value. The spread below therefore comes only from mass, area and the wave terms.

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

standing_checks.limiting_factor: reachable launch speed 0.67 m/s is 11.36 m/s below v_min 12.04 m/s: lift cannot carry the weight

equations: W = m g; v_min = sqrt(2 W / (rho S C_Lmax))

launch speed v0 = the organism's own: adult flying fish = taxi end speed 15 m/s (leap ~10 m/s then taxi; lower end of the measured 15-20 m/s); other flying-fish stages min(10 m/s, 30 BL/s x SL), no taxi; zebrafish Umax = 1.15 Ucrit; otherwise not evaluated
cannot glide if v0 < v_min: every range = 0, feasible = false
Lean-covered part: d_lean = h (L/D)max   (glide_range_le: d <= h (L/D)/(1 - delta))
kinetic phase (outside the theorem): x_A = (L/D)_eff (v0^2 - v_min^2)/(2g), (L/D)_eff = (L/D)max / f_ground(h/(b/2))

model_honesty.statement: STUDIO-FINDINGS.md's one honest sentence applies to everything above: every numeric wild-type value that lands in band is read straight from the paper it is scored against. The negative controls (a zebrafish that cannot glide, a wingless flying fish that cannot glide, a TFF that cannot pay for powered flight) are the part of this result that is NOT circular, because they turn on inequalities between independently sourced quantities rather than on a fitted number.

physics_simulation.scope: Whether the design DOES the function asked of it, measured by running the engine's own scenario modules. It is not a validity claim and it is not a statement that the design is biologically possible: lean_check says no law is broken (necessary, not sufficient) and this says the function is or is not achieved in the model. Every check carries the validation status of the model behind it, and a check whose model is `circular` -- scored against a number read back from the paper it is compared with -- is not evidence however green it looks. The ensemble is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION over stated input distributions, most of whose shapes are assumed; it is not a measured distribution of real behaviour. Control, flapping, unsteady aerodynamics, take-off power, adhesion and whole-body stability are not modelled anywhere in this engine.

report.gates_note: lean_check says the design BREAKS NO LAW, which is necessary and not sufficient. physics_simulation says whether it ACTUALLY DOES THE THING. Neither substitutes for the other, and neither is folded into the score.

criteria.source_text: inferred: a realistic glide. 10 m from a 1 m launch, inside the 5-75 m band the independent harness scores the real flying fish against (STUDIO-RESULTS W9: 36.5 m at 15 m/s, pass-rests-on-assumed)

per_stage.stage_label: adult, 365 d after hatching, SL 206.2 mm

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band applies to this animal at this stage

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

equations: W = m g; v_min = sqrt(2 W / (rho S C_Lmax))

launch speed v0 = the organism's own: adult flying fish = taxi end speed 15 m/s (leap ~10 m/s then taxi; lower end of the measured 15-20 m/s); other flying-fish stages min(10 m/s, 30 BL/s x SL), no taxi; zebrafish Umax = 1.15 Ucrit; otherwise not evaluated
cannot glide if v0 < v_min: every range = 0, feasible = false
Lean-covered part: d_lean = h (L/D)max   (glide_range_le: d <= h (L/D)/(1 - delta))
kinetic phase (outside the theorem): x_A = (L/D)_eff (v0^2 - v_min^2)/(2g), (L/D)_eff = (L/D)max / f_ground(h/(b/2))
total = d_lean + x_A (labelled as not covered by the theorem)
P_req = W v_min / (L/D)max; P_aerobic <= eta E_O2 Q C_a(PO2)

sources.cite: Park H, Choi H (2010). Aerodynamic characteristics of flying fish in gliding flight. J Exp Biol 213:3269-3279

Makiguchi Y et al. (2013). Take-off performance of flying fish Cypselurus heterurus doederleini measured with miniature acceleration data loggers. Aquat Biol 18:105-111 (leap speed ~10 m/s, 20-30 BL/s, citing Davenport 1994; glide up to 50 m at 15-20 m/s citing Edgerton & Breder 1941)

Deng J et al. (2019). Numerical prediction of aerodynamic performance for a flying fish during gliding flight. Bioinspir Biomim 14:046009 (maximum flight height 8 m; average taxiing length 9 m, second-hand)

Deng J, Wang S, Zhang L, Mao X (2019). Why does a flying fish taxi on sea surface before take-off? A hydrodynamic interpretation. bioRxiv 765560 (taxiing accelerates to 15-20 m/s, citing Davenport 1994)
Durnford FPH, Porter ES, Gamperl AK (2026). Increased heart rate and blood oxygen extraction ... schoolmaster snapper. J Exp Biol
Rummer JL, Brauner CJ (2015). Root effect haemoglobins in fish ... PLoS One 10:e0139477
Gerry SP, Ellerby DJ (2014). Resolving shifting patterns of muscle energy use in swimming fish. PLoS One 9:e106030

criteria.source_text: inferred: lift must carry the weight at the launch speed the animal can actually reach

per_stage.stage_label: adult, 365 d after hatching, SL 206.2 mm

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band applies to this animal at this stage

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

model_honesty.statement: STUDIO-FINDINGS.md's one honest sentence applies to everything above: every numeric wild-type value that lands in band is read straight from the paper it is scored against. The negative controls (a zebrafish that cannot glide, a wingless flying fish that cannot glide, a TFF that cannot pay for powered flight) are the part of this result that is NOT circular, because they turn on inequalities between independently sourced quantities rather than on a fitted number.

physics_simulation.scope: Whether the design DOES the function asked of it, measured by running the engine's own scenario modules. It is not a validity claim and it is not a statement that the design is biologically possible: lean_check says no law is broken (necessary, not sufficient) and this says the function is or is not achieved in the model. Every check carries the validation status of the model behind it, and a check whose model is `circular` -- scored against a number read back from the paper it is compared with -- is not evidence however green it looks. The ensemble is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION over stated input distributions, most of whose shapes are assumed; it is not a measured distribution of real behaviour. Control, flapping, unsteady aerodynamics, take-off power, adhesion and whole-body stability are not modelled anywhere in this engine.

report.gates_note: lean_check says the design BREAKS NO LAW, which is necessary and not sufficient. physics_simulation says whether it ACTUALLY DOES THE THING. Neither substitutes for the other, and neither is folded into the score.

per_stage.limiting_factor: cannot glide: the reachable launch speed 0.67 m/s is below v_min 8.64 m/s, so lift cannot carry the weight [achieved in 0.0 % of 200 draws over the stated input distributions; median 0 m, 5-95 % 0 to 0]
per_stage.out_of_validity: Mass 0.0006943 kg is outside 0.02-0.4 kg (polar specimens 0.04-0.06 kg; field fliers to ~0.4 kg): polar extrapolated. Mean-chord Reynolds number ~3.1e+3 is outside 5e3-1e5 around the polar's Re ~1e4 (Park & Choi: 'gliding flying fish (Re ~10^4)'; air kinematic viscosity 1.46e-5 m2/s). glide_range_total_m exceeds the Lean bound whenever the kinetic phase is non-zero; only glide_range_lean_bound_m is covered by glide_range_le. Fick bound: arterial PO2 taken equal to air PO2 and gills taken to work in air; gills do not ventilate in air (physiology chain), so for a gill-breather this is a generous upper bound. TFF: NOTES-FOR-HUB.md item 2 says only 29.5% of the flight muscle the simulator charges fits in the body. This module uses no muscle power (the Fick bound is the cap), so the issue does not enter here; any muscle-based claim for the TFF must take it into account.

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band does NOT apply: no sourced launch-speed spread for this animal, so the launch speed is NOT drawn and stays at the engine's own value. The spread below therefore comes only from mass, area and the wave terms.

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

equations: W = m g; v_min = sqrt(2 W / (rho S C_Lmax))

launch speed v0 = the organism's own: adult flying fish = taxi end speed 15 m/s (leap ~10 m/s then taxi; lower end of the measured 15-20 m/s); other flying-fish stages min(10 m/s, 30 BL/s x SL), no taxi; zebrafish Umax = 1.15 Ucrit; otherwise not evaluated
cannot glide if v0 < v_min: every range = 0, feasible = false
Lean-covered part: d_lean = h (L/D)max   (glide_range_le: d <= h (L/D)/(1 - delta))
kinetic phase (outside the theorem): x_A = (L/D)_eff (v0^2 - v_min^2)/(2g), (L/D)_eff = (L/D)max / f_ground(h/(b/2))
total = d_lean + x_A (labelled as not covered by the theorem)
P_req = W v_min / (L/D)max; P_aerobic <= eta E_O2 Q C_a(PO2)

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band does NOT apply: no sourced launch-speed spread for this animal, so the launch speed is NOT drawn and stays at the engine's own value. The spread below therefore comes only from mass, area and the wave terms.

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

equations: W = m g; v_min = sqrt(2 W / (rho S C_Lmax))

launch speed v0 = the organism's own: adult flying fish = taxi end speed 15 m/s (leap ~10 m/s then taxi; lower end of the measured 15-20 m/s); other flying-fish stages min(10 m/s, 30 BL/s x SL), no taxi; zebrafish Umax = 1.15 Ucrit; otherwise not evaluated
cannot glide if v0 < v_min: every range = 0, feasible = false
Lean-covered part: d_lean = h (L/D)max   (glide_range_le: d <= h (L/D)/(1 - delta))
kinetic phase (outside the theorem): x_A = (L/D)_eff (v0^2 - v_min^2)/(2g), (L/D)_eff = (L/D)max / f_ground(h/(b/2))
total = d_lean + x_A (labelled as not covered by the theorem)
P_req = W v_min / (L/D)max; P_aerobic <= eta E_O2 Q C_a(PO2)

model_honesty.statement: STUDIO-FINDINGS.md's one honest sentence applies to everything above: every numeric wild-type value that lands in band is read straight from the paper it is scored against. The negative controls (a zebrafish that cannot glide, a wingless flying fish that cannot glide, a TFF that cannot pay for powered flight) are the part of this result that is NOT circular, because they turn on inequalities between independently sourced quantities rather than on a fitted number.

physics_simulation.scope: Whether the design DOES the function asked of it, measured by running the engine's own scenario modules. It is not a validity claim and it is not a statement that the design is biologically possible: lean_check says no law is broken (necessary, not sufficient) and this says the function is or is not achieved in the model. Every check carries the validation status of the model behind it, and a check whose model is `circular` -- scored against a number read back from the paper it is compared with -- is not evidence however green it looks. The ensemble is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION over stated input distributions, most of whose shapes are assumed; it is not a measured distribution of real behaviour. Control, flapping, unsteady aerodynamics, take-off power, adhesion and whole-body stability are not modelled anywhere in this engine.

report.gates_note: lean_check says the design BREAKS NO LAW, which is necessary and not sufficient. physics_simulation says whether it ACTUALLY DOES THE THING. Neither substitutes for the other, and neither is folded into the score.

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band applies to this animal at this stage

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

equations: W = m g; v_min = sqrt(2 W / (rho S C_Lmax))

launch speed v0 = the organism's own: adult flying fish = taxi end speed 15 m/s (leap ~10 m/s then taxi; lower end of the measured 15-20 m/s); other flying-fish stages min(10 m/s, 30 BL/s x SL), no taxi; zebrafish Umax = 1.15 Ucrit; otherwise not evaluated
cannot glide if v0 < v_min: every range = 0, feasible = false
Lean-covered part: d_lean = h (L/D)max   (glide_range_le: d <= h (L/D)/(1 - delta))
kinetic phase (outside the theorem): x_A = (L/D)_eff (v0^2 - v_min^2)/(2g), (L/D)_eff = (L/D)max / f_ground(h/(b/2))
total = d_lean + x_A (labelled as not covered by the theorem)
P_req = W v_min / (L/D)max; P_aerobic <= eta E_O2 Q C_a(PO2)

criteria.source_text: inferred: it must at least glide; 10 m is well inside the 5-75 m band the independent harness scores the real animal against (STUDIO-RESULTS W9)

per_stage.stage_label: adult, 365 d after hatching, SL 206.2 mm

species_gate.note: the 15-20 m/s taxi band applies to this animal at this stage

sea_state.source: NO sea state exists anywhere in this repository. Hs 1.0 m and wavelength 30 m are a modelling choice (a "slight" wind sea) chosen so the wave terms are small next to the 1 m default launch height. sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs states explicitly: "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)", so these two numbers are the first time a wave surface is given any role, and they are assumed, not measured.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.
